entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Federal Center of Technological Education Celso Suckow da Fonseca (CEFET-RJ), established in 1917 in Brazil, represents a pivotal development in the country's educational landscape, particularly in the realm of technological and vocational training. Located in the state of Rio de Janeiro, this institution was named after Celso Suckow da Fonseca, a prominent figure in Brazilian education who advocated for technical education as a means to modernize the workforce. CEFET-RJ's founding coincided with a period of industrialization in Brazil, emphasizing the necessity for skilled labor to support burgeoning sectors such as manufacturing and services, thereby cementing its significance in the broader narrative of Brazil's economic evolution.

Throughout its history, CEFET-RJ has expanded its offerings to include a range of technical and higher education programs, producing thousands of graduates who have contributed to various fields, including engineering, information technology, and environmental science. The institution has been instrumental in the promotion of research and innovation, often collaborating with industries to address practical challenges and integrate cutting-edge technology into its curriculum. Notably, during the 1960s and 70s, CEFET-RJ became a hub for technological advancement, aligning its programs with national development plans to enhance Brazil's position in the global economy.
